title: INVESTIGATE — Scorch decals approach research (revert DecalGeometry attempt, evaluate 6 alternatives, pick simplest viable)
intent: Dev hit blockers implementing GDP-2026-05-29-001 (Three.js DecalGeometry-based scorch marks). User asked to revert + spike out alternatives. This INVESTIGATE story spec'd to (1) revert any DecalGeometry work-in-progress, (2) evaluate 6 known approaches to floor scorch marks, (3) prototype the simplest viable, (4) pick the approach to ship + file the implementation story. NO ship work in this story — produces a written analysis + a small working spike. Outputs: `docs/research/scorch-decals-spike.md` covering all 6 approaches + verdict.
rationale: Source: user feedback — dev cannot produce 'normal scorch trail from exploded bomb' with the DecalGeometry approach from GDP-2026-05-29-001. The original story proposed Three.js DecalGeometry — a known correct technique for STATIC meshes but fragile when target meshes get re-spawned (which they do via Wang autotile re-resolve, soft-block destruction, height changes). Spike to find the right approach before committing implementation effort. Cheap research story; high-value output (unblocks scorch + footstep marks).
acceptanceHints: OUTPUT: written analysis at `docs/research/scorch-decals-spike.md` covering 6 approaches + recommended path + minimal working prototype.

STEP 1 — REVERT any in-progress DecalGeometry implementation. Dev's failed attempt likely lives on a branch — close that PR + clean up partial code. GDP-2026-05-29-001 stays in archive as 'attempted, deferred — see GDP-2026-05-30-004'.
STEP 2 — RESEARCH the 6 known approaches. Document trade-offs for each:
APPROACH 1 — Three.js DecalGeometry (what didn't work):
Three.js `DecalGeometry(targetMesh, position, orientation, size)` projects a small mesh onto an existing target.
PROS: conforms to target surface (handles slopes, ramps if target geometry curved).

CONS: requires STABLE target mesh — when Wang autotile re-resolves (soft block destroyed → 4 neighbours re-spawn meshes), the decal's target mesh disappears. Decal floats orphan or crashes. Also: per-decal Three.js geometry allocation + dispose = GC churn.
VERDICT: dropped. Right tool for static meshes; wrong for our dynamic-cell pipeline.
APPROACH 2 — Simple plane entity at cell top (RECOMMENDED v1):
Each scorch = a small thin plane entity (BoxGeometry 1×0.005×1) parented at the cell's top face.
Y position = cell.height + 0.01 (slight float to avoid Z-fighting with floor).
Vertex-color dark warm scorch (#1a0a05) at full opacity, tween to 0 over lifetime via existing Tween primitive.
For multiple blasts on same cell: multiple ScorchTile entities stack additively — darkens over time.

PROS: simplest possible. Reuses BlastTile pattern (S82 — already a thin plane entity). Wang autotile re-resolves don't break (ScorchTile is its OWN entity, not projected onto floor mesh). Cuboid cells with variable height handled trivially (read cell.height).
CONS: doesn't conform to cliff face sides (only top faces). Doesn't follow uneven terrain (we don't have uneven terrain — all cells are cuboid with flat tops, so this is fine for our case).
VERDICT: recommended. Closes user request with minimum implementation cost.
APPROACH 3 — Vertex-color overlay on existing cell mesh:
Directly modify the existing cell mesh's per-vertex colour buffer at the moment of blast.
PROS: zero new entities, zero extra draw calls. Decal IS the floor.

CONS: cell meshes are SHARED via the procedural-mesh-registry (S101 cache). Modifying one cell's vertex colours either modifies all instances (catastrophe) or requires un-sharing the mesh (defeats the cache). Wang autotile re-resolves wipe the modifications.
VERDICT: not viable without breaking mesh cache.
APPROACH 4 — Shader uniform per cell (scorch intensity):
Custom floor material reads a per-cell scorchIntensity uniform (or per-instance attribute via InstancedBufferGeometry).
PROS: real-time, no extra geometry, integrates with future post-FX.
CONS: significant shader work. Per-cell uniform = expensive (uniform per draw call). Per-instance attribute requires InstancedMesh refactor of the entire floor render path. Heavy.
VERDICT: deferred. Future polish when post-FX pipeline lands.
APPROACH 5 — Render-to-texture floor 'splat' atlas:
Maintain a per-arena texture (e.g. 256×256 or arena-size×8 resolution) onto which scorch is rendered as the round progresses. Floor material samples this texture.
PROS: industry-standard (Destiny, Doom, etc.). Persistent across round. Smooth blending between decals.
CONS: heavy. Render-to-texture path doesn't exist in Three.js without explicit setup. Requires careful UV mapping per cell. Performance hit ~2-3ms / frame.
VERDICT: deferred. Significant new render-pipeline surface. Worth considering for MVP-4 polish.
APPROACH 6 — InstancedMesh pool of decal quads:

Pre-allocate one InstancedMesh of N decal quads (e.g. N=200). Each instance has position + age uniform. Scorch system allocates an unused instance per blast, updates per-instance attributes (Transform, opacity).
PROS: ONE draw call for all decals. Pooled — no GC churn. Per-instance opacity tween.
CONS: requires InstancedMesh refactor. Fixed pool size — N decals max simultaneously. Slightly trickier to bind per-instance opacity attribute.
VERDICT: deferred. Worth revisiting if Approach 2 shows perf issues at scale (50+ simultaneous decals). For our scale (~20 max), Approach 2 is sufficient.

STEP 3 — PROTOTYPE Approach 2 (simple plane entity). Minimal working code: spawn a ScorchTile entity at a chosen blast cell, fade over 3s. Validate it Wang-autotile-survives + visible + despawns clean.
STEP 4 — RECOMMENDATION DOC. Final section of `scorch-decals-spike.md`:
Recommended approach: Approach 2 (simple plane entity, BlastTile pattern).
Why: simplest implementation, reuses proven entity pattern from S82 BlastTile, no Wang interference, handles variable height trivially.
Path forward: file `GDP-2026-05-30-005` (implementation) using the prototype as reference. ~100 LOC + tests.
Cliff-face scorch (where projection would matter) explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for v1 — flat-top scorch only. Can revisit with Approach 4 (shader) or 5 (splat) when MVP-4 polish lands.
STEP 5 — FILE the implementation story. Reference this investigation as the source.
DELIVERABLES:
docs/research/scorch-decals-spike.md (this story's main output)
Working prototype branch (kept ephemeral OR merged as 'spike disabled by default' behind feature flag)
New story filed: GDP-2026-05-30-005 — implementation of Approach 2
OUT OF SCOPE:
Production implementation of any approach — only spike research + prototype.
Cliff-face decals — flat tops only in any approach.
Footstep marks (mentioned in GDP-2026-05-29-001) — same approach applies; ship in the implementation story.
Multi-arena persistence (scorch carries between rounds). Out — round-scoped only.
Decals on bomber meshes (damage marks on bodies). Future polish.
